headline: 20-of-24 beat Miami. Crosby is the next snap.
dek: Kansas City is 3-0 after a 24-10 win at Hard Rock Stadium, and the tape that actually travels — 88 rushing yards, 3-of-7 on third down, 25:39 with the ball — now meets a 3-0 Raiders club on Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT.
videoHook: They won 24-10 in Miami and still lost the clock by nine minutes. Both clubs are 3-0. The next snap is Las Vegas, and Maxx Crosby already called the meeting.
theEdge: ESPN FPI at 70.2 percent and DraftKings hanging Chiefs -5.5 on a 47.5 total is a road-favorite number against another 3-0 AFC West team, not a bye — Polymarket’s 8.6 percent Super Bowl price and 16.0 percent AFC ticket are what you get when a 3-0 club wins 24-10 while losing first downs, third downs, and nearly nine minutes of football.

storyline.lede: The scoreboard in Miami said 24-10 and the record says 3-0, but the possession tape said the Dolphins were the ones living in Kansas City’s huddle. Patrick Mahomes went 20-of-24 for 246 yards and two touchdowns, Kenneth Walker III added 70 yards and the 10-yard score that opened it, and still the Chiefs left Hard Rock Stadium with 18 first downs, 88 rushing yards, and 25:39 with the ball. That is the film Steve Spagnuolo and Eric Bieniemy have to carry into a division road game against a Raiders team that is also 3-0 and already hearing Maxx Crosby’s warning.
body: Miami finished with 19 first downs, 119 rushing yards, 8-of-16 on third down, and 34:21 of possession. The Dolphins did not win. They did win the math that usually decides January. Kansas City answered with explosive throws — Travis Kelce’s 48-yard strike on the opening series, Rashee Rice’s 34-yarder in the fourth quarter, Noah Gray’s 24-yarder to the 8 — and with two takeaways, L. Sneed’s fumble recovery and Karlaftis intercepting Malik Willis. Efficiency covered a run game that stalled and a defense that kept jogging back on the field.

That is the uncomfortable 3-0. Last year’s 6-11 club taught this building what happens when the supporting tape never catches the quarterback. This year’s supporting tape is closer: Walker is a real back, Rice is a real volume receiver, and the defense can still create the ball. It is not yet the tape of a team that can survive Crosby crashing the pocket while the offense is 3-of-7 on third down.

Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT in Las Vegas is the first true AFC West measuring stick of 2026. ESPN FPI posts Kansas City at 70.2 percent. DraftKings hangs the Chiefs -5.5 on a 47.5 total. Those are favorite numbers, not immunity. The Chargers already sit three games back, which makes this Raiders game a chance to own the division early or to hand a 3-0 rival the same seat. The assignment is simple to say and hard to run: get the ball back, run it better than 88, and keep Mahomes from taking the beating he took in Miami.

lastGameReview.label: Week 3 · Sun, Sep 27 · 12:00 PM CT
lastGameReview.lede: Kansas City scored in the first two minutes when Walker, with J. Moore reported eligible, went up the middle for a 10-yard touchdown after Mahomes hit Kelce for 48 yards, then spent the rest of the afternoon trading punches with a Dolphins offense that kept the ball. Miami tied it 7-7 on a 3-yard touchdown, the Chiefs answered with a 5-yard touchdown for 14-7, and the second half became a clock fight: Miami’s 37-yard field goal made it 14-10, Kansas City’s 34-yard field goal made it 17-10, and an 11-yard touchdown at 2:55 of the fourth quarter finally made it 24-10.

analysis.body: The opening series was the version of Andy Reid’s offense everyone came to see. Under center, a deep-middle shot to Kelce to the Miami 19, then Walker through the A-gap for the 10-yard score. From there the run game lost the line of scrimmage. Walker still finished 18 carries for 70 yards, but the team managed only 88 on the ground, and the drive that died at the Miami 12 — two Walker runs for no gain, the second with H. Nourzad eligible — was the snapshot. He also lost six yards on a right-end toss in the fourth quarter, so this was not a between-the-tackles identity that simply got stacked. It was a run game that could not finish.

Mahomes’ 20-of-24 is the number that travels on television. The complementary number is the punishment he took to post it, and the interception he threw at the two-minute warning of the second quarter, a deep-middle ball for Rice that J. Rodriguez took back 18 yards to the Miami 47. Play-action still created the look Kansas City wants: Thornton and Worthy both won 17-yard shots down the sideline, Gray’s 24-yarder set up the 34-yard field goal, and Rice’s 34-yard catch to the Miami 15 preceded the 11-yard touchdown that closed it. Accuracy covered protection. It will not cover Crosby.

Spagnuolo’s defense won the score and lost the field. After the Chiefs’ two-minute opening strike, Miami answered with a 17-play grind that ate nearly 9.5 minutes and tied the game, and Spagnuolo pulled the unit aside. Nick Bolton finished with 11 tackles and lived in the run fits; the Dolphins still ran for 119. The splash plays were real: L. Sneed forced and recovered Willis’s fumble after Kansas City challenged the down-by-contact ruling, and Karlaftis intercepted Willis short right with Chris Jones in the throwing lane to ice the possession fight. Those are championship takeaways. They had to be, because Miami converted 8-of-16 third downs and Kansas City converted 3-of-7.

The finishing tape is mixed on purpose. Harrison Butker’s 34-yarder made it 17-10; his 50-yarder at 0:57 sailed wide left. Miami turned it over on downs twice in incomplete-pass situations, once to M. Delane and once to N. Williams. Kansas City did not dominate a team it was supposed to put away. It made enough explosive throws and enough takeaways to leave 3-0 with a 24-10 road win that still requires a grown-up meeting before Las Vegas.

takeaways.title: Efficiency covered a lost clock
takeaways.body: Mahomes at 20-of-24 for 246 and two touchdowns is how you win 24-10 with 25:39 of possession. Miami’s 34:21 and 19 first downs are how you get honest about the next opponent. Las Vegas will not gift that completion percentage if the run game stays at 88.

takeaways.title: Takeaways, not third down, closed Miami
takeaways.body: Sneed’s forced fumble and recovery, then Karlaftis intercepting Willis, are the two possessions Kansas City stole. The Dolphins still won third down 8-16 to 3-7. Spagnuolo can live with splash plays. He cannot live with that conversion gap against a 3-0 division rival.

takeaways.title: The run game has an identity problem, not a back problem
takeaways.body: Walker’s 70 yards on 18 carries included the 10-yard touchdown, interior work, and end runs that cut both ways, including the minus-6. The team number is 88. That is not enough to keep play-action honest when Crosby is the next man in the backfield.

whatWorked: Mahomes’ 20-of-24, 246-yard, two-touchdown day, including the deep-middle shot to Kelce that set up Walker’s 10-yard score
Play-action creating clean looks for Thornton, Worthy, Gray, and Rice down the field
L. Sneed forcing and recovering Willis’s fumble after the replay challenge
Karlaftis intercepting Willis at the Miami 36 to snuff a late drive
Rice’s 7 catches for 88 yards as the volume outlet when the run stalled
whatDidnt: Team rushing stuck at 88 yards, with Walker stuffed for no gain on consecutive snaps at the Miami 12 and a turnover on downs
Third down at 3-of-7 while Miami went 8-of-16 and held the ball 34:21
The interception Rodriguez took off Mahomes on the deep-middle ball for Rice
Protection that let Mahomes take too many hits for a 20-of-24 afternoon
Penalties (Tr. Smith, R. Thomas, L. Sneed, Karlaftis) and Butker’s 50-yard miss that kept the clock conversation alive

currentState.lede: Kansas City is 3-0 with wins over Denver, Indianapolis, and Miami, sitting tied with Las Vegas atop the AFC West, and still carrying the same two open items from Hard Rock Stadium: a run game that finished with 88 yards and a defense that could not get off the field on third down. The quarterback is playing at a champion’s completion rate. The supporting tape is playing at a favorite’s, not a juggernaut’s.

workOn.title: Get the run game past 88
workOn.body: Walker’s 70 on 18 is a feature-back line. The team’s 88 is a problem against a Raiders front that will let Crosby wreck early downs if Kansas City has to throw from behind the sticks. Inside zone has to win first down on Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT, or play-action becomes a costume.

workOn.title: Third-down offense and third-down defense
workOn.body: Going 3-of-7 while the opponent goes 8-of-16 is how you post 25:39 of possession in a win. Spagnuolo already had to pull the unit aside after Miami’s opening grind. Las Vegas will script the same long drives if the second level does not rally and if the offense cannot stay on schedule.

workOn.title: Keep Mahomes off the ground
workOn.body: Twenty-of-24 does not erase the hits. Screens, boots, and a committed run game are how Bieniemy keeps the quarterback upright against Crosby. If the protection plan is five-man dropback, the 3-0 start will start quoting last year’s 6-11 in a hurry.

thinkAbout.title: Is 3-0 a style or a scoreboard?
thinkAbout.body: The Colts game produced 152 rushing yards and 37:00 of possession. Miami produced 88 and 25:39. Both are wins. Only one of those tapes survives Crosby and a 3-0 Raiders locker room that just got a blunt warning about this trip.

thinkAbout.title: How much blitz is too much from Sneed?
thinkAbout.body: The Week 3 snap counts made L’Jarius Sneed a featured blitzer, and he forced the fumble that flipped a series. Simulated pressure is Spagnuolo’s signature. It also walked Kansas City into holding and illegal-use flags. The Raiders game is where that dial either becomes a weapon or a self-inflicted down-and-distance problem.

thinkAbout.title: What the market is actually buying
thinkAbout.body: ESPN FPI at 70.2 percent and Chiefs -5.5 on 47.5 is respect. Polymarket at 8.6 percent to win the Super Bowl and 16.0 percent to win the AFC is probation. A division road game against a 3-0 club is how that gap either shrinks or gets quoted back to the fan base.

gamePlan.lede: Both clubs are 3-0 and tied atop the AFC West, and Kansas City is a 5.5-point road favorite on CBS at Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT. The assignment is to bring a heavier early-down identity than the 88-yard Miami tape and to keep Maxx Crosby from turning Mahomes’ 20-of-24 efficiency into a survival drill.
gamePlan.howTheyMatch: Kansas City wants to live in play-action and let Mahomes throw with a clean platform. Las Vegas wants to make every dropback a Crosby snap and dare the Chiefs to run into a loaded box. Walker versus that front is the leverage point: if he can push the team number north of Miami’s 88, Kelce and Rice become answers instead of necessities. If he cannot, Spagnuolo’s defense — which just spent 34:21 on the field — will be asked to win another low-possession game on the road.

keys.title: Boot and screen Crosby, do not sit on him
keys.body: Play-action boot away from Crosby and RB screens off the aggressive upfield rush are the two ways to cash the Miami passing tape without asking the tackles to win a 40-drop game. Mahomes already took too much punishment. This is how you stop repeating it.

keys.title: Win first down so third down is not 3-of-7 again
keys.body: Inside zone to Walker, with an extra lineman when Reid wants the same jumbo look that scored from 10 yards in Miami, has to create 2nd-and-5. Mesh to Rice and Kelce is the third-down answer if Las Vegas sits man. The Chiefs cannot live in 3rd-and-long on the road in this division.

keys.title: Get off the field without waiting on a takeaway
keys.body: Sneed’s fumble and Karlaftis’s interception won Miami. They are not a plan. Cover-2 to take the lid off, then simulated pressure with Sneed and a dropping lineman on money downs, is how Spagnuolo shortens the Raiders’ drives before the clock looks like 34:21 again.

script: Open in 13 personnel with an extra lineman and Walker on inside zone — copy the Miami scoring look without waiting until you trail the sticks.
Second series: under-center play-action boot away from Crosby, Kelce leaking, Worthy as the deep-over answer.
Early RB screen to Walker or the backup when Crosby wins upfield; make the Raiders rush pay for the same aggression that punished Mahomes in Miami.
Third-and-medium: mesh with Rice and Kelce rubbing, Noah Gray sitting, Walker as the checkdown.
Defensively, start in a Cover-2 shell on early downs to keep the ball in front after Miami just posted 19 first downs.
On 3rd-and-5 or longer, zone-blitz with Sneed from the slot and a dropping end so Jones and Karlaftis are not asked to win every rush on their own.

nextGame.label: Week 4 · Sun, Oct 4 · 3:25 PM CT
nextGame.note: Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT — 3-0 at 3-0 in the AFC West, Chiefs -5.5

spotlight.title: Mahomes was perfect enough, and still too available
spotlight.body: Twenty-of-24 for 246 and two touchdowns is a clinic. The hits he took to post it are the clip Crosby will watch. Kansas City can stay 3-0 on the road only if the answers are boots and screens, not another 40-drop survival tape.

spotlight.title: Walker’s 70 cannot stay a team 88
spotlight.body: Eighteen carries, 70 yards, and the 10-yard touchdown are feature work. End runs cut both ways, including the minus-6, and the two stuffed snaps at the Miami 12 killed a red-zone series. Las Vegas is where the interior identity has to show up.

spotlight.title: Sneed created one, Karlaftis closed one
spotlight.body: L. Sneed forced and recovered Willis’s fumble after the challenge. Karlaftis intercepted Willis short right with Jones in the picture. Those two possessions are why 25:39 of offense still produced 24 points. They are not a substitute for getting off the field on third down.

spotlight.title: Crosby already crashed the party
spotlight.body: The Raiders are 3-0 and tied with Kansas City. Crosby made sure the celebration came with a warning about this Chiefs trip. That is the correct temperature for a road favorite that just lost the clock in Miami.

spotlight.title: The Chargers are already three back
spotlight.body: A win in Las Vegas would put Kansas City in position to own the AFC West before the Chargers even arrive in Week 6. A loss hands a 3-0 rival the same seat. The market’s 70.2 percent is not the same thing as a comfortable week.

matchups.chiefs: Mahomes’ protection and Bieniemy’s boot/screen package
matchups.note: Miami already put too many hits on a 20-of-24 afternoon. Crosby is the cleaner edge rusher, and Kansas City has to move the pocket or the 3-0 record becomes a dropback problem.

matchups.unit: Walker and the interior run vs. Raiders front
matchups.chiefs: Kenneth Walker III (18-70-1) plus the extra-lineman looks
matchups.note: Team rushing was 88 in Miami. Walker can still win a snap; the line has not proven it can win a series. This is the snap that decides whether play-action is real.

matchups.unit: Mahomes to Rice/Kelce vs. Raiders coverage
matchups.chiefs: Patrick Mahomes, Rashee Rice (7-88), Travis Kelce
matchups.note: Kelce’s 48-yarder and Rice’s 34-yarder were the explosive answers when the run stalled. If Las Vegas sits man, mesh is the call. If they sit two-deep, the underneath work has to replace the 88 rushing yards.

matchups.unit: Spagnuolo front vs. Raiders early downs
matchups.chiefs: Chris Jones, Karlaftis, Nick Bolton (11 tackles)
matchups.note: Jones and Karlaftis still wreck protection, and Karlaftis just took the ball away. The concern is volume: Miami ran for 119 and held it 34:21. Bolton has to fit cleaner if the offense stays off the field.

matchups.unit: Sneed as blitzer vs. Raiders protection
matchups.chiefs: L’Jarius Sneed (forced and recovered the Willis fumble)
matchups.note: The snap-count tape made Sneed a featured blitzer, and he cashed a fumble. Flags came with the extra heat. Spagnuolo needs the simulated look, not the penalty look, on the road.

xsandos.title: Jumbo inside zone, copy the 10-yard scoring look
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, opening series at Las Vegas, extra lineman in the game
xsandos.why: Kansas City just ran for 88 as a team in Miami and still needed Mahomes at 20-of-24 to win. Walker’s 10-yard touchdown came with J. Moore eligible; the two stuffed snaps at the Miami 12 came when the same jumbo look lost the line. Against a 3-0 Raiders front, early-down zone is how you keep Crosby from pinning Mahomes in 3rd-and-long.
xsandos.coaching: Walker has to press the heel of the center and take the one cut — the minus-6 on the right-end toss is the cut you do not bring to this game. Nourzad and the extra lineman must win the double on the three-technique so Bolton’s counterpart cannot walk into the backfield free.

xsandos.title: Play-action boot away from Crosby
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-5 after a Walker zone run, Crosby aligned over the left tackle
xsandos.why: Play-action was the cleanest part of the Miami passing tape, and Mahomes still took too much punishment sitting in the pocket. Booting him to the opposite hash turns Crosby’s upfield rush into a pursuit angle and recreates the easy-throw platform that produced Kelce’s 48-yarder and Gray’s 24-yarder.
xsandos.coaching: Bieniemy has to sell the zone fake with the same footwork as the inside-zone series or Crosby will not bite. Kelce leaks, Worthy runs the over, and Mahomes’ first read is the flat — throw it before the pursuit, do not reset into the rush he just escaped in Miami.

xsandos.title: Mesh to Rice and Kelce on third down
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-6, Chiefs needing to bury the 3-of-7 Miami tape
xsandos.why: Kansas City converted 3-of-7 in Miami and still won because Rice (7-88) and Kelce created chunk gains on schedule. If Las Vegas plays man to take away the deep shot, the rub between Rice and Kelce is the conversion answer that keeps Mahomes from another hit-and-hope dropback.
xsandos.coaching: Rice owns the right-to-left rub and has to flatten at five yards, not climb into the linebacker. Kelce takes the opposite mesh and sits if the Mike drops. Walker is the outlet — Mahomes checked it down in Miami when the pocket collapsed; take the same throw and live.

xsandos.title: Walker screen when Crosby climbs
xsandos.situation: 2nd-and-7, Raiders showing five-man pressure with Crosby wide
xsandos.why: The Miami tape said Mahomes can complete anything if he is upright, and it also said he will not stay upright if the plan is five-man protection. A perimeter screen to Walker — who already handled 18 touches — punishes Crosby’s upfield takeoff and replaces some of the 88 rushing yards without asking the interior to win a phone booth.
xsandos.coaching: The left tackle must whiff on purpose and climb to the safety, not chase Crosby. Gray and the playside guard are the actual lead blockers. Walker has to let the throw arrive; the minus-6 end run is what happens when he accelerates before the wall is set.

xsandos.title: Cover-2 shell, keep the ball in front
xsandos.situation: 1st-and-10, Raiders coming off their own 3-0 tape, early down in Las Vegas
xsandos.why: Miami just posted 19 first downs, 119 rushing yards, and 34:21 of possession, including a 42-yard shot to Dulcich through the middle of the field. Spagnuolo’s two-deep, five-under shell is how you take that shot away and make Bolton and Tranquill rally, instead of living on the splash plays from Sneed and Karlaftis.
xsandos.coaching: Safeties split the posts and do not cheat the run until the mesh point. Bolton fits inside-out and finishes the 11-tackle work he posted in Miami. Corners funnel to the two-deep; the miss is the vertical from the slot, not the tackle after the catch.

xsandos.title: Sneed simulated pressure, drop the end
xsandos.situation: 3rd-and-5, Raiders in shotgun, money down after Miami went 8-of-16
xsandos.why: The snap-count tape made L’Jarius Sneed a featured blitzer, and he forced and recovered a fumble playing downhill. Spagnuolo cannot wait on another Karlaftis interception to get off the field. Showing heat, dropping a lineman, and sending Sneed from the second level is the call that shortens drives against a 3-0 offense without asking Jones to win every snap as a four-man rush.
xsandos.coaching: Sneed’s path is the A-gap or the slot seam — do not clip the tackle and pick up the illegal-use flag that wiped a late Miami interception look. The dropping end has to land in the throwing lane Willis kept missing in Miami. Jones still occupies two blockers; Karlaftis rushes off the opposite edge so the quarterback’s hot throw has nowhere clean to go.

coaching.topic: Reid and Bieniemy have to script the run they did not finish
coaching.detail: The 10-yard jumbo score was the identity. The stuffed snaps at the Miami 12 were the week’s problem. Las Vegas is not the place to hope 20-of-24 shows up again without an early-down run plan.
He pulled the defense aside after Miami’s opening 17-play grind. The next version of that meeting has to happen on the sideline in Las Vegas, not after another 34:21 possession tape.

The Raiders’ 3-0 celebration came with Crosby’s warning about this Chiefs trip. Reid’s staff should treat that as the scouting report: the edge is coming, and the answers are boots, screens, and first-down runs.

personnel.move: L’Jarius Sneed as a featured blitzer
personnel.detail: Week 3 snap counts showed Sneed used as heat, and he forced and recovered Willis’s fumble. That package should travel to Las Vegas as long as the flags travel home.
Eighteen carries, 70 yards, and the 10-yard touchdown make him the run-game answer. The staff still needs a second-man change of pace after the two no-gain snaps and the minus-6 end run.

personnel.move: Extra linemen in the scoring package
personnel.detail: J. Moore eligible on the 10-yard touchdown and Nourzad eligible on the stuffed red-zone snaps are the same personnel idea with two different results. Clean up the second look before Crosby sees it on film.

strategies: Commit to inside zone on the opening series so play-action is a threat, not a costume, against Crosby.
Move Mahomes off the launch point with boots and Walker screens to avoid repeating the Miami punishment tape.
Use Rice-Kelce mesh as the third-down staple instead of another deep-middle shot into traffic like the Rodriguez interception.
Start Spagnuolo in Cover-2 on early downs to erase the 42-yard middle shot Miami hit, then mix Sneed’s simulated pressure on money downs.
Protect the football after the one Mahomes interception; a minus-one game on the road against a 3-0 rival is how 5.5-point favorites get hunted.
Treat the clock as a statistic you can lose and still win once — Miami’s 34:21 is not a plan you bring into the AFC West.
debates: If you had one game ball from 24-10, is it Mahomes at 20-of-24, Walker’s 10-yard score and 70 yards, or Sneed’s forced fumble?
Does 3-0 with 88 rushing yards and 25:39 of possession feel like a contender or like a favorite living on the quarterback?
Should Spagnuolo keep featuring Sneed as a blitzer after the fumble and the flags, or sit him in coverage against Las Vegas?
Is Chiefs -5.5 on 47.5 the right number for a 3-0 at 3-0 division game, or is ESPN FPI at 70.2 percent too high after the Miami clock tape?
What has to change before the Chargers arrive in Week 6 — the run game, the third-down defense, or Mahomes’ protection?

runOfShow.talkTrack: Twenty-of-24, 24-10, 3-0 — and still 88 rushing yards and 25:39 with the ball. Hold the graphic of Walker’s 10-yard score next to Miami’s 34:21. Then cut to Crosby’s warning. That is the episode.

Walk the scoring sequence in order: Walker 10 yards for 7-0, Miami 3 yards for 7-7, Chiefs 5 yards for 14-7, Miami 37-yard field goal for 14-10, Chiefs 34-yard field goal for 17-10, Chiefs 11 yards for 24-10. Then the real tape: 18 first downs, 3-of-7, Sneed’s fumble, Karlaftis’s interception, the stuffed snaps at the 12.

Contrast the Colts game’s 152 rushing yards and 37:00 with Miami’s 88 and 25:39 without blending the boxes. Mahomes, Kelce, and Walker are covering imperfections. Ask whether that coverage survives a 3-0 Raiders front.

Lay the six cards: jumbo inside zone, boot away from Crosby, mesh on third down, Walker screen, Cover-2 shell, Sneed zone blitz. Hit the market: ESPN FPI 70.2 percent, DraftKings -5.5 on 47.5, Polymarket 8.6 percent Super Bowl and 16.0 percent AFC.
Crosby versus the tackles is the edge they do not own. Rice and Kelce versus man is the edge they do. Close with the game-ball question and the Chargers sitting three back heading toward Week 6.
Sun Oct 4, 3:25 PM CT, CBS, both clubs 3-0. Remind them the score in Miami was 24-10 and the clock was not. Send them to the site for the cards.
